title: Frontend queue + API/SDK state consistency (F3)
implemented_items: GET /api/v1/kb/jobs (new, additive) lists durable jobs for the caller with durable FIFO queue_position/queued_total per namespace, newest-first for the UI.

job_status projection on POST /ingestion-jobs (202), GET /jobs/{id} and POST /jobs/{id}/cancel adds phase (queued/parsing/written/indexing/ready/draft_ready/retry/failed/cancelled/unknown), task_id, namespace_id, document_id, revision, progress_known/processed_units/total_units (null unless a real pair exists), retryable, resume_granularity, alignment_status, structure_source, fallback_strategy, artifact_uri, trace_id, error, warnings, heartbeat. Existing durable fields and the 202/GET contract are preserved.

Empty queue never reported as ready: phase is derived only from durable state; 'written' is distinct from 'indexing' and 'ready'; ready is only ever the explicit durable state (job_complete still refuses to fabricate ready).

Frontend: web-studio/src/routes/tasks/-lib/durable-job.ts (types, normalize, fetch, queue-position/progress/fallback formatting, queue summary); -components/durable-jobs-panel.tsx wired into the tasks route; monitoring durable-queue-card.tsx + labels prop on queue-status-card.tsx wired into the monitoring queue tab.
Permission + trace: job listing filters to the caller account/principal and re-runs KBJobService.get ACL checks per job; trace_id surfaced for log correlation.

test_commands.covers: queued Nth-in-line + FIFO renumber, unknown progress, written/indexing/ready transitions, failed/retry/cancelled, fallback notice persistent, empty queue != ready, state survives authority store re-open, cross-principal invisibility
no regression to the existing durable-job and wiki-ingestion HTTP contract

test_commands.command: cd web-studio && node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/routes/tasks/-lib/durable-job.test.ts src/routes/tasks/route.test.tsx src/routes/monitoring
test_commands.covers: durable job projection helpers and existing tasks/monitoring suites

test_commands.result: no errors in any touched/new frontend file; repo-wide pre-existing errors remain in unrelated files (gen/ov-client, settings, resources, retrieval, etc.) and in pre-existing unused-var warnings inside tasks/route.tsx

not_run: Full UI acceptance in a real browser (TC-3.6 C-layer): no browser/e2e run was executed, so visual rendering, live polling and permission-filtered rendering are NOT verified end-to-end.
Sync/async SDK wait-timeout reattach against a live worker is NOT_RUN; only the HTTP read path that a reattach would use is covered.
Real worker-driven written->indexing->ready transitions over a running parse backend are NOT_RUN; transitions were driven through the authority repository commands directly.
Multi-namespace fairness/priority scheduling under load (TC-3.7 I-layer) is NOT_RUN; only single-namespace FIFO ordering is asserted.
Cross-restart persistence was verified by re-opening the authority store in-process, not by restarting a real server process.
follow_ups: openviking/indexing/jobs.py was read-only per footprint. The durable store has no queue-position query and no namespace-scoped count; the router computes positions from job_list. A dedicated bounded query (e.g. job_queue_state(account, namespace)) would avoid listing up to 1000 rows per status read.

KBJobService has no authorized list command; the router lists via repository.job_list then re-checks each job through KBJobService.get. A first-class service.list() would be cleaner and avoid the per-job ACL round trip.

job_status reads checkpoint/info keys (processed_units, total_units, alignment_status, structure_source, fallback_strategy, artifact_uri, resume_granularity, trace_id) that no producer currently writes for D1/D2 ingestion; the fields stay null/unknown until the executor populates them.
notes: No other module was modified; openviking/indexing/jobs.py and openviking/service/* were read only.
The frontend durable client fails soft to an empty list on transport error so an unreachable surface is not rendered as a ready/empty queue.
